title: bn254-gt-dlp: gated digit-tag 6-adding rho, 144 instructions per certified step, window 1280, expected work 2^118.98

claims.statement: For uniform z=g^x in the protected BN254 GT (g=e(P0,Q0) from target-profile.json, x uniform in [0,r)), the gated digit-tag 6-adding distinguished-point Pollard rho of proof.md (selector coordinate t = the real part of the w^1 coefficient, which no nontrivial Frobenius power fixes; a point Y is distinguished iff t(Y) 2^84 < p, the same 84-bit predicate in the algorithm, the caps and the ledger) returns x with g^x=z with probability at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh coins, at EXPECTED total work at most 1 + (K/2^64)(144 E[T] + 9216 (E[T]/1280 + E[walks] + 1) + 1792 E[X] + 2^110)/20000 < 2^118.98 reference units (W=R/20,000, R total scalar AArch64 instruction-equivalent work; T steps and X exact evaluations of a run past the gate). This is an expectation over the challenge and the coins of the one attack on the one target, not a bound on every run; every run, including all failures, is capped at 2^132.96 units by a 2^140-step global three-word step counter, at most 2^52 walks of at most 2^90 steps, at most 2^127 exact evaluations, at most 2^70 store probes and at most 1,024 draws per random scalar. The attack first draws a fresh uniform 64-bit word v and stops as a failure unless v < K = 7237656125499723472, the least K with (K/2^64) x 0.994 >= 0.39; past the gate it runs to its first verified recovery and succeeds with probability at least 0.9945 (failure budget below 0.0055: step cap at most 0.000158 and walk cap at most 0.005037 by Markov's inequality, exact-evaluation meter at most 0.000276, all other caps and degenerate events below 2^-19). The certified-tag method and the table of all products of at most ell multipliers are those of submission 73463878-0c19-4309-a991-749ea525d51c, whose reference.py, experiment.py, listings and development evidence are included byte for byte except DP_BITS = 84 in experiment.py and the dbits=84 docstring in reference.py. The digit tag (the window base as 72 digits of 43 bits, one 64-bit entry word per digit, tag error below 72 x 2^43) and the 6-adding configuration with long windows are those of submission 70974bf7-180b-47e1-a09b-c88363cfa805, adopted with credit; the gate and run-to-collision expected-work accounting follow 8b901b3d-a617-4b1f-a442-ff370e6ec4f7; the unrolled loop follows f86cff50-80c5-43cf-a773-67417a7c29e4. New here: the Frobenius-free selector coordinate; a generated digit loop of 144 executed scalar AArch64 instructions per certified step (walks.py part S, 18 resident digits, encoding-validated and executed trip by trip against the definition with all exits exercised); exact evaluation from a row v(T_e) stored in every entry by a generated 1,294-instruction routine without re-base, charged 1,792 at the uncertified rate (14 2^48 + 2)/2^64 = 2^-12.19; compact non-leaf entries, so the window length is ell = 1280 (C(1286,6) = 6,209,268,427,492,417 table entries, peak storage below 2^63 bytes); a generated 171-instruction digit conversion; and this account's generated 8,679-instruction lazy-reduction window product. A window end costs at most 9,216 instructions and a step costs 144 + 9216/1280 + 1792 (14 2^48 + 2)/2^64 <= 151.59 instructions in expectation. The digit tag lemma is checked on window bases produced by the generated programs (part T, with a Frobenius check of t), and a 120-step full-width walk on real table entries runs through the generated loop, product and digit conversion with 14 window ends and 0 mismatches, the generated exact evaluation agreeing with the true t at every check (part I). The expected work uses E[T] <= 1.08 sqrt(pi kappa r/2) + 2^85 <= 2^127.3667 steps, kappa = 6/5 (premise H-mean on the mean collision time of the 6-adding walk, with H1 and the restricted equidistribution premise H2r of proof.md section 6 over first visits to inversion pairs, which also gives the revisitation-aware distinguished-point argument), supported by toy-scale runs of the complete 6-adding walk (development-evidence-mean6.json: means rising from 0.923 at 16 bits to about 1.01-1.02 at 28-36 bits; Pooled at n >= 28 bits: 3,840 runs, mean 1.0129, s.e. 0.0085; mean + 3 s.e. = 1.0384) and extrapolated to production size. Table construction (below 2^73 instructions) and all other work are included without amortization. Peak storage is below 2^63 bytes, nonuniform advice 0 bytes. No production-size run is claimed; this is a generic square-root attack, not a security estimate.

experiments.purpose: Part C: assert that submission.json, proof.md and machine.md state one 84-bit distinguished-point predicate, the same parameters as the code, and rounded bounds on the safe side of the ledger. Part S: generate the digit tag loop, validate the encoding of every instruction and execute it trip by trip on synthetic table entries against the definition (A, selector, child, exits). Part L: generate the lazy-reduction window-end Fp12 product and the digit conversion as a straight-line scalar AArch64 program with asserted static bounds, validate the encoding of every instruction, execute it on an instruction simulator and compare with big-integer arithmetic. Part T: check the tag certificate in this layout on window bases produced by that routine. Part H: toy-scale runs of the complete 6-adding distinguished-point walk run to recovery, mean collision time against sqrt(pi kappa n/2). Part I: a full-width walk on real table entries through the generated loop, product, digit conversion and exact evaluation, checked step by step against the definition. Part X (declared input only): assert that every experimental figure stated in the manifest, proof.md and machine.md equals this run's measured value. Part G: gate, caps, failure budget and expected-work ledger in exact decimal arithmetic. Then execute the base package's experiment.py (submission 73463878; changed only to DP_BITS = 84) in-process: tower and row checks, tag certificate on 260 cases, 120-step full-width walk (steps_wanted = 120), toy runs at the cap, listing recount. Toy runs are evidence at their own scale only.
